log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Whimsicott
Light Screen ended on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Incineroar FakeOut/Intimidate + Whimsicott Tailwind control speed. Lucario-Mega Adaptability sweeper in back with Garchomp as secondary fast attacker. Handles Dragapult speed with Tailwind, resists Fairy/Dragon with Steel typing.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Dragapult (Scarf), Gholdengo (LifeOrb), Grimmsnarl (Prankster/Light Clay), Floette-Eternal (Mega), Rotom (Leftovers), Absol (FocusSash). Need Tailwind for speed control. Lucario-Mega is primary win condition.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Lucario-Mega. Lead Grimmsnarl + Dragapult applies Fake Out and sets dual screens, pressuring the foe while Lucario-Mega hits hard. Backline Gholdengo + Rotom provides fast offense, Will-O-Wisp support, and pivot options to keep momentum. Floette-Eternal stays in base form for backline flexibility and to avoid overcommitting to Mega tempo.
decisions.notebook: Core strategy centers on Grimmsnarl's Prankster Fake Out and dual screens, with Dragapult providing speed control and pivot options. Gholdengo brings strong special offense (Make It Rain) and coverage, while Rotom adds Will-O-Wisp and Hex synergy; Floette-Eternal offers Protect for tempo and a flexible backline. Mega plan targets Lucario-Mega; Floette-Eternal remains base for backline stability. If Tailwind arrives from Whimsicott, rely on Dragapult's speed and Rotom pivots to maintain pressure; adapt to Incineroar Fake Out and Krookodile threats as needed.

decisions.rationale: Secure Tailwind for Lucario win condition. Flinch Grimmsnarl to prevent Prankster screens/parting shot. Dragapult is fast but Whimsicott has Sash.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Rotom)
decisions.rationale: Placing Light Screen now shields Rotom/Grimmsnarl from special hits and lets Rotom burn Incineroar to blunt its physical pressure. This preserves Grimmsnarl for future screens and pivots into Gholdengo. Rotom's burn also reduces Incineroar's offense while you build backline pressure with Make It Rain and Dragapult pivots.

Prepare to switch Grimmsnarl to Gholdengo next turn to establish Make It Rain pressure and continue dual-screen common-sense tempo. Target Lucario-Mega as the primary late-game threat; Lucario-Mega's arrival will shape your switch-or-press timing. Maintain Tailwind awareness and use Protect/priority to manage tempo.

decisions.rationale: Switch Grimmsnarl to Dragapult to preserve speed leverage and maintain light-screen utility; Rotom passes to preserve momentum and avoid unnecessary exposure. Dragapult offers instant tempo and a path to heal/retaliate without sacrificing screens or Burn pressure. Rotom’s Will-O-Wisp pressure remains on Garchomp and Lucario.

Expect Lucario-Mega to enter on a pivotal turn; aim to keep speed parity via Tailwind cues and Dragapult’s rapid repositioning. If Grimmsnarl is back in, prioritize setting a second screen as needed and use Rotom for chip and pivot options. Prepare for Incineroar Parting Shot to shift momentum and for Garchomp brn-heavy pressure as a closing threat.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Earthquake hits ally and is ineffective vs Rotom. Dragapult Choice Scarf OHKOes Garchomp with super-effective Dragon moves. Switching to Lucario-Mega saves Garchomp; Lucario-Mega resists Dragon and is immune to Ghost. Parting Shot lowers Dragapult's stats. Lucario-Mega can attack with Close Combat.

reflections.summary: Lost due to matchup disadvantage: Tailwind expired before Lucario-Mega could outspeed Dragapult Scarf, and Garchomp was choice-locked into Earthquake against Rotom's Levitate.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Lucario-Mega with a faster threat or speed control that outspeeds Dragapult Scarf without relying on Tailwind duration.
reflections.notebook: Dragapult Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Darts. Rotom pivots with VoltSwitch and uses Will-O-Wisp frequently. Gholdengo is a target for Earthquake but can switch to Rotom. Grimmsnarl Prankster threat. Lucario-Mega requires Tailwind to outspeed Dragapult Scarf. Incineroar Protect streak is risky.

reflections.summary: The game was lost because a scarf Garchomp pressured the board and landed a critical hit that removed a key setup piece (Gholdengo), after Mega Lucario had already been knocked out. The plan to deny Mega evolution and pivot to Gholdengo did not counter the opponent’s late‑game tempo, and Dragapult ended up locked into Dragon Darts, limiting options against a fast, scarfed threat.
reflections.adjustment: Do not rely on a locked-in Dragon Darts path against scarf targets. Switch Dragapult to a non-locked set (e.g., Life Orb or another flexible role) to preserve offensive options and keep a credible Garchomp check. Prioritize maintaining Rotom’s Will-O-Wisp to cripple Garchomp early and preserve momentum with Gholdengo.
reflections.notebook:
Opponent tendencies:
- Prefers Garchomp + Mega Lucario cores, using scarf Garchomp to outspeed and threaten Earthquake; Protects Lucario to stall.
- May employ Tailwind via Whimsicott to boost tempo; aims to pressure and pivot into stronger late-game threats.
Revealed strategic facts:
- A critical hit on Gholdengo by Garchomp swung the game; burn on Garchomp reduced its punch but wasn’t enough to stop the sweep.
- Mega Lucario arrived and was knocked out; Dragapult with Scarf ended up locked into Dragon Darts on the critical turns, limiting tempo management.
Future plans:
- Against this opponent, plan to counter scarf Garchomp with a non-locked Dragapult or an alternative fast check, and rely on Rotom’s Will-O-Wisp to blunt Garchomp’s offense earlier.
- Use Gholdengo as a momentum driver, but ensure a reliable early-game counter to Garchomp and avoid giving the opponent a sustained tempo edge.
